Design contrasts for conditional within-between slopes

Source: R/slopes.R
wb_slope_design.Rd

Integration hook for the S3 methods in interactions::sim_slopes(). Uses the same hypothetical-grid transformation as interaction plots. No models are refitted, and no person means are recomputed from the grid.

Usage

wb_slope_design(
  model,
  pred,
  grid,
  cond.int = FALSE,
  check_support = TRUE,
  linear.moderator = NULL
)

Arguments

model

A fitted wbm or wbgee model, optionally prepared by prepare_wb_plot() to use within-person display units.

pred

Character name of an untransformed numeric focal predictor.

grid

A data frame containing all predictor values for each requested profile, on the selected display scale. Without plotting metadata, inputs use original units and original levels.

cond.int

Will conditional intercepts be reported? If so, their location at pred = 0 on the display scale is checked for extrapolation. Intercept design rows and offsets are returned regardless.

check_support

Warn about out-of-range profile values? Internal unit steps used to calculate contrasts never trigger extrapolation warnings.

linear.moderator

Optional moderator name that must enter linearly, as required for analytic Johnson-Neyman regions.

Value

A list containing slope contrasts (L), intercept design rows (X0), intercept offsets, fixed-effect coefficients, their covariance matrix, residual degrees of freedom, and the number of observations.

Details

Slopes are fixed-effect, link-scale slopes conditional on reference person means and interaction-centering quantities. They are not derivatives of an entire recomputed panel history, nor averages over random effects. The Gaussian identity link gives response-scale slopes. Predictor units follow the display scale even when the fitted model is standardized. Nonlinear focal terms, predictor-dependent offsets, basis expansions, lagged/detrended models, and rank-deficient fits are not supported.
